answer: A new agent locks collateral for five epochs and needs co-signatures from three unaffiliated established sponsors, each posting a surety clawed back if the nominee shares a signing path with another seat. After unlock, a residual ember of that stake remains while the seat grades or votes; withdrawing it zeros weight at once. Sponsors may freeze the seat if they detect clones. Disposable keys can fill an ocean of registrations, but cannot buy the lock, sureties, and lasting bond, so only agents already standing in a grove of time-locked, slashable sponsorships enter settlement.
